questions.prompt: Partition sizes are [100, 120, 80, 110, 450]. Using Spark AQE's default factor of 5 (and a tiny byte threshold), is the last partition skewed?
options: Yes, it's more than 4x the mean
No: the median is 110, and 450 is less than 5 × 110 = 550
Yes, any partition above the median is skewed
It can't be decided without the key distribution
questions.explanation: AQE compares against the median, not the mean. 450 < 550, so it isn't flagged.

questions.prompt: You salt a hot key into 8 sub-keys, compute partial sums per (key, salt), and stop. What's wrong?
options: Nothing, the partial sums are the answer
The hot key now has up to 8 partial rows. A second phase must add them per key to get the exact total
You must use a mean instead
questions.explanation: Salting spreads the work but also splits the result. Phase 2 drops the salt and adds the partials.

questions.prompt: In a salted join, the big side's hot key rows get salts 0..7. What must happen to the matching rows on the small side?
options: They also get a random salt
Each is replicated 8 times, once per salt
questions.explanation: A big-side row tagged (k, s) only meets small-side rows tagged (k, s), so every salt needs its own copy.

questions.prompt: A table is partitioned as year=YYYY/month=MM. Which predicate lets the engine skip whole directories?
options: None: directories are always all read
questions.explanation: Only predicates on partition columns can rule out a directory from its path. Filters on other columns need data skipping statistics or a full scan.
